$comment: DERIVED, not verbatim. Written by this library from the prose of SLSA VSA v1.2 section 6 (SlsaResult), with section 3.2 (verifiedLevels). Source: .cache/slsa-vsa-1-2.txt (SLSA v1.2 spec/verification_summary.md, releases/v1.2 @ ae7fc76, sha256 71adb7cc46a537c5a9b81fa8b14ae11cbc61ac91cc62c66197d1c1da8d92ccb0), line numbers L are in that rendering. GRAMMAR as stated (L375-397): an SlsaResult SHOULD be SLSA_<TRACK_NAME>_LEVEL_<LEVEL_NUMBER> (the SLSA Track level the artifact qualifies for) or SLSA_<TRACK NAME>_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED (R-0014, R-0076, R-0077); the examples are SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_UNEVALUATED, SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_0, SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_3, SLSA_SOURCE_LEVEL_2, SLSA_SOURCE_LEVEL_4 and FAILED (L385-390); custom values are permitted but none may start with SLSA_ (R-0080, R-0081, L396-397). verifiedLevels may also carry verified properties (L196), SLSA-endorsed values defined outside this source (L402-404). READING: a string in the level form, that is one that starts with SLSA_ and has _LEVEL either at its end or followed by an underscore, must match the track-level pattern; any other string is accepted: FAILED, the verified properties and any other SLSA-endorsed value (in v1.2 SLSA_SOURCE_TWO_PARTY_REVIEWED and SLSA_BUILD_REPRODUCED, named on SLSA's verified-properties page at ae7fc76, outside this source), and custom values. Whether a SLSA_ string outside the level form is an endorsed value or a forbidden custom one can be decided only against SLSA's own list of values, so it is not bound here (SILENT tests). Pass 1's version applied the pattern to every string starting with SLSA_, and so rejected both v1.2 verified properties; pass 2 narrowed the if. The source writes the track placeholder both as <TRACK_NAME> (L379) and <TRACK NAME> (L380) and never defines track names or the range of <LEVEL_NUMBER>: the pattern takes upper-case letters, digits and underscores for the track and decimal digits for the number, so SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_03 and SLSA_BUILD_LEVEL_LEVEL_3 are accepted; no level maximum is bound. Lower-case strings (slsa_build_level_1) do not start with SLSA_ and so count as custom values. OUTSIDE THIS SOURCE: which tracks exist and what each level means (the SLSA Track definitions), and the verified properties. The one-level-per-track rule of verifiedLevels is not expressible here: see check-schemas.derived.py semantic rule SEM-01.
